parsed.rationale: Although both `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` and `TimeShiftablePlayer` live in the same `Playback` package and share a handful of method names (`installRenderTap`, `removeRenderTap`, `isPlaying`, `stop`, `play`), the structural evidence explicitly reports `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, indicating the pipeline found no formally shared slots. More importantly, the two protocols encode distinct domain responsibilities: `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` is a low-level AVAudioEngine rendering interface (exposing `scheduleBuffer`, `scheduleBuffers`, `makeRenderTapStream`, `volume`) while `TimeShiftablePlayer` is a higher-level time-shifting playback contract (exposing `seek`, `seekToLive`, `secondsBehindLive`, `maxLookbackSeconds`, `isAtLiveEdge`, `stateStream`, `timePositionStream`). Introducing a shared parent protocol would force every `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` conformer to satisfy time-shifting semantics it has no business implementing, and vice versa; the surface overlap in method names (`play`, `stop`, `installRenderTap`) is coincidental to their respective abstraction layers rather than evidence of a genuine shared contract.
